title: Monetary Policy Report—January 2025
summary: The Bank of Canada reduced its overnight rate by 25 basis points to 3% and announced an end to quantitative tightening, reflecting confidence that inflation has remained around the 2% target. The Bank forecasts Canadian economic growth to average 1.8% in 2025 and 2026, with excess supply expected to gradually dissipate. A major source of uncertainty is the threat of new US tariffs, which is already weighing on consumer and business confidence and contributing to Canadian dollar depreciation.
key_points: Bank of Canada cut the overnight rate target to 3% (Bank Rate at 3.25%, deposit rate at 2.95%), a 25 basis point reduction
Quantitative tightening has ended; this marks a shift in the Bank's balance sheet policy
Inflation has been around 2% since August 2024 and is projected to remain near target over the projection horizon
Canadian GDP growth forecast: 1.8% in both 2025 and 2026
US tariff threats are identified as a major source of uncertainty affecting confidence, investment, and the Canadian dollar
Shelter price inflation remains elevated despite overall moderation in price pressures
The outlook does not incorporate new US tariffs, though the Bank provides an illustrative scenario analyzing potential tariff impacts
why_it_matters: This quarterly report provides the official framework for Canadian monetary policy and signals the Bank of Canada's priorities: supporting growth while maintaining inflation near 2%. The rate cut and end of QT represent a pivot toward easing, while the explicit acknowledgment of tariff uncertainty sets the context for future policy decisions. Markets and analysts use this report to calibrate expectations for the Canadian dollar, bonds, and rate-sensitive sectors.
macro_context: Canada's economy shows modest excess supply with a soft labour market and some signs of slowing wage growth. Past interest rate cuts are beginning to support household spending and housing activity. The global economy is expected to grow at around 3%, with US growth remaining strong in 2025 before moderating in 2026. Euro area growth is subdued while China shows near-term strength from policy measures. Both upside and downside risks to the inflation outlook are considered roughly balanced, with trade policy emerging as a major uncertainty.
important_numbers: 1.8% - forecast Canadian GDP growth for 2025 and 2026
2% - inflation target and current inflation level

issues_found: Minor phrasing: summary states 'inflation has returned to the 2% target' while source says 'has been around 2%' and 'remains close to 2%' — 'returned to' is slightly more assertive than the source language
